scholar_status: The identifier is linked in the existing repository. Direct retrieval was blocked (HTTP 429), so this is not a verified export of the complete Scholar profile.
completeness: Eighteen distinct works are supported by the existing site and primary project, author, laboratory, arXiv, or publisher sources. This includes a separately listed challenge technical report and the recent survey added following Zi Wang’s correction. No exhaustive completeness claim is warranted because Scholar could not be retrieved.
selected_rule: Include papers where Zi Wang is first author or explicitly marked as an equal-contribution co-first author, plus explicitly selected collaborations. The current selection contains six (co-)lead-authored papers and SONIC, a collaboration selected by Zi Wang.

papers.title: Large Discrete Policy: Advancing Explicit Behavior Modeling with Stochastic Iterative Scoring
papers.summary: A discrete policy selects plausible actions through repeated stochastic scoring and candidate pruning.
papers.notes: The project page supplies the author list; the first author's current homepage lists NeurIPS 2026. Zi Wang has no equal-contribution mark.

papers.title: Beyond Textual Chain-of-Thought: A Survey on Action-Grounded Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: A survey of 171 papers organizing action-grounded reasoning for autonomous driving into language-based, visual-spatial, latent-dynamic, and externalized representations.
papers.figure_alt: Survey overview: four reasoning representations connect a driving scene to an action, illustrated by yielding to a pedestrian.
papers.notes: Added after Zi Wang noted his missing recent survey. ACL Anthology confirms Findings of EMNLP 2026; the official paper marks Zhengxu Tang and Xiaozhou Zhang as equal contributors. Zi Wang is fifth author, so this paper appears in All. The project link is a curated paper collection, not model implementation code.

papers.title: ENPIRE: Agentic Robot Policy Self-Improvement in the Real World
papers.summary: Coding agents improve physical robot policies through automated resets, rollouts, verification, and algorithm refinement.
papers.notes: EMBER and co-first author Jia Xie explicitly list CoRL 2026 and the equal-contribution authors. Zi Wang is not one of them.

papers.title: GRAIL: Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from World Models
papers.summary: Video world models generate humanoid training interactions grounded in known 3D scenes for visual sim-to-real learning.
papers.notes: NVIDIA's project page explicitly marks four Co-First Authors and CoRL 2026 Oral Presentation. Earlier title: GRAIL: Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from 3D Assets and Video Priors. Use the current project title.

papers.title: HAD: Combining Hierarchical Diffusion with Metric-Decoupled RL for End-to-End Driving
papers.summary: Hierarchical diffusion and metric-decoupled reinforcement learning improve end-to-end driving trajectories.
papers.notes: A secondary site labels this ECCV 2026, but no primary venue confirmation was obtained. Keep arXiv until verified. The author block does not mark Zi Wang as equal first.

papers.title: SONIC: Supersizing Motion Tracking for Natural Humanoid Whole-Body Control
papers.summary: Scaling motion data, model capacity, and compute produces a generalist humanoid whole-body controller.
papers.notes: The current GEAR-SONIC project page and arXiv v4 agree on 28 authors: the first five are co-first authors (†), the next nine including Zi Wang are core contributors (*), and the last two provide equal advising (‡). Zi Wang is a core contributor, not co-first. SONIC is explicitly selected as a collaboration.

papers.title: Opening the Sim-to-Real Door for Humanoid Pixel-to-Action Policy Transfer
papers.summary: An RGB-based humanoid policy learns door-opening skills in simulation and transfers to varied real-world doors.
papers.notes: The project page explicitly marks the first three authors equal contribution. Tairan He's site lists CVPR 2026. EMBER's author list additionally includes Ye Yuan, conflicting with arXiv and the project page; prefer project/arXiv.

papers.title: VIRAL: Visual Sim-to-Real at Scale for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.summary: Large-scale visual simulation trains humanoid loco-manipulation policies that transfer directly to real hardware.
papers.notes: The project explicitly marks the first four authors equal contributions. Tairan He's current homepage lists CVPR 2026.

papers.title: Zero-Human Demonstration End-to-end Autonomous Driving with Trajectory Scorer
papers.summary: Trajectory scoring and exhaustive policy optimization enable end-to-end driving without human demonstrations.
papers.notes: arXiv v2 and project have a new title and 12-author list. The first author's homepage lists this same work under its former ZTRS title as ECCV 2026. An aggregator labels ICLR 2026; do not use that unsupported venue.

papers.title: DriveSuprim: Towards Precise Trajectory Selection for End-to-End Planning
papers.summary: Coarse-to-fine candidate filtering improves precise trajectory selection for end-to-end planning.
papers.notes: The arXiv comments explicitly say accepted to AAAI 2026.

papers.title: Reinforcement Fine-tuning of End-to-end Trajectory Scorers
papers.summary: Reinforcement fine-tuning adapts trajectory scorers for closed-loop driving in photorealistic simulation.
papers.notes: The first author lists this separately from GTRS and ZTRS. The venue description is Driving Simulation from Real-World Data, Closed-Loop Driving in Photorealistic Simulation. This is a challenge report, not a main-conference paper.

papers.title: Generalized Trajectory Scoring for End-to-end Multimodal Planning
papers.distinction: 1st Place, CVPR 2025 Autonomous Grand Challenge, End-to-end Driving
papers.summary: Generalized trajectory scoring combines coarse and fine candidate evaluation for multimodal driving plans.
papers.notes: arXiv comments identify the first-place challenge solution.

papers.title: Enhancing Autonomous Driving Safety with Collision Scenario Integration
papers.summary: Collision scenario generation and safety-oriented training improve planning in collision-prone driving scenes.
papers.notes: Zi Wang is first author. IROS is confirmed by coauthor homepage; Oral is retained from Zi Wang's existing site.

papers.title: ASAP: Aligning Simulation and Real-World Physics for Learning Agile Humanoid Whole-Body Skills
papers.summary: A learned residual action model aligns simulated physics with real hardware for agile humanoid motion.
papers.notes: RSS 2025 is in arXiv comments. Zi Wang is fifth author and is not marked equal contribution in the existing author list.

papers.title: Editable Scene Simulation for Autonomous Driving via Collaborative LLM-Agents
papers.summary: Collaborating language-model agents edit photorealistic driving scenes from natural-language instructions.
papers.notes: The project explicitly marks the first four authors equal contribution and CVPR 2024 Highlight. The CVF record confirms the full eight-author list. Existing site incorrectly omits Hao Zhao and Yanfeng Wang.

papers.title: DialogueNeRF: Towards Realistic Avatar Face-to-Face Conversation Video Generation
papers.summary: A neural radiance field models speakers and listeners to generate face-to-face avatar conversations.
papers.notes: Publisher author block marks only Yichao Yan and Zanwei Zhou with the equal-contribution note. Published August 7, 2024, volume 2, article 24.

papers.title: Interruption-Aware Cooperative Perception for V2X Communication-Aided Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: Historical cooperative information helps recover missing perception messages during V2X communication interruptions.
papers.notes: arXiv explicitly gives IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles 2024. No evidence of Zi Wang co-first authorship was found.

papers.title: TBP-Former: Learning Temporal Bird's-Eye-View Pyramid for Joint Perception and Prediction in Vision-Centric Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: A temporal bird’s-eye-view pyramid combines spatial and temporal features for joint perception and prediction.
papers.notes: The paper HTML explicitly says Shaoheng Fang and Zi Wang contributed equally. The arXiv version includes Yanfeng Wang, but the first author's homepage, USC laboratory publication list, and CVPR bibliographic listing use the five-author conference version. Retain the five-author conference version.

reference_design_observations: Tairan He's current site uses compact biography and links, a short news list, then publication entries with authors, venue, project/PDF links, abstracts, and BibTeX. The reference content is current enough to confirm VIRAL and DoorMan as CVPR 2026.
